content.thinking: This deployment introduced an O(n^2) performance bug in average_spend_per_item, recomputing the running sum in a nested loop instead of a simple division, and the latency spike lines up exactly with the 15:34:00Z deploy time. This confirms it's a bad code deployment causing a genuine performance regression, not a config issue, since CPU work now scales quadratically with purchase count.

hypotheses.subject: average_spend_per_item in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py
hypotheses.summary: The 15:34:00Z deploy of revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655 replaced a constant-time division (account.total_cents // len(purchases)) with a nested loop that recomputes the running sum of purchases on every iteration, making average_spend_per_item O(n^2) in the number of purchases. This lines up exactly with the onset: p50/p95/p99 latency jump from ~45/215/380ms to ~277-450/1300-2200/2400-3900ms starting at the 15:34 bucket, the same minute the deploy landed, while request volume and CPU/memory stay flat. The resulting slow account-page renders caused shoppers to time out and disconnect ('ClientDisconnected' errors visible in the logs from 15:33 onward, worsening after the deploy), which the alert reported as elevated error/latency.

supporting_evidence.claim: modified src/io_shop/spend_summary.py: '- return account.total_cents // len(account.purchases)' replaced with a per-purchase loop recomputing 'spent_by_then' each iteration before the same final division
